data.title: Total Revenue by Region
data.explanation: This chart ranks all regions by their total revenue. The highest-earning regions are shown at the top, based on summed consultation and retail revenue from the financial summary.
data.code: SELECT r.RegionName, SUM(f.TotalRevenue_GBP) AS TotalRevenue_GBP FROM fact_financial_summary f JOIN dim_region r ON f.RegionID = r.RegionID GROUP BY r.RegionName ORDER BY TotalRevenue_GBP DESC
insights: Edinburgh leads all regions with £726K revenue, outpacing second-place Birmingham by ~£48K.
Top 3 regions (Edinburgh, Birmingham, London South) are tightly clustered within £63K of each other.
Cardiff is the lowest performer at £391K, roughly half of Edinburgh's revenue.
Both London regions combined (£1.24M) exceed Edinburgh's total by 70%, showing strong capital presence.
recommendations: Investigate Edinburgh's success factors and replicate winning strategies in underperforming regions like Cardiff and Bristol.
Consider consolidating London North and South reporting to better target the combined £1.24M market opportunity.
Prioritise stylist recruitment or marketing spend in Cardiff and Newcastle to close the gap with top regions.

marcus.title: Revenue trend over the last 9 months

data.title: Revenue Trend – Last 9 Months
data.explanation: This line chart shows total revenue aggregated across all consultants for each of the last 9 months, allowing you to spot growth trends, seasonal dips, and momentum shifts over the period.
data.code: SELECT Year, MonthNum, SUM(TotalRevenue_GBP) AS TotalRevenue_GBP, CAST(Year AS VARCHAR) || '-' || LPAD(CAST(MonthNum AS VARCHAR), 2, '0') AS MonthLabel FROM fact_financial_summary GROUP BY Year, MonthNum ORDER BY Year DESC, MonthNum DESC LIMIT 9
insights: Peak revenue was £154,006 in Nov 2025; lowest was £117,669 in Jan 2026 — a £36,337 gap.
Revenue declined sharply from Nov 2025 peak (£154k) to Jan 2026 trough (£118k), dropping ~24%.
March 2026 shows a recovery to £135,666, the strongest month in 2026 so far.
Jul–Aug 2025 were stable (~£146k each), suggesting summer is a consistently solid period.
recommendations: Investigate Jan 2026 drop drivers (post-holiday slump?) and implement early-year booking incentives.
Capitalise on March 2026 momentum by launching Q2 promotions to sustain the recovery trend.
Replicate Nov 2025 tactics — likely seasonal gifting or events — to boost future Q4 revenue.
data.forecast: The recovery from the Jan 2026 trough to £135,666 in March is encouraging, suggesting Q2 2026 could return toward the £145k–£150k range seen in mid-2025 if momentum holds.

marcus.title: Create a stacked bar chart of monthly revenue from January to December, with each bar split into 4 territory segments and show the total on top of each bar.

data.title: Monthly Revenue by Region (2024)
data.explanation: This stacked bar chart shows total monthly revenue for 2024 split across all regions. Each coloured segment represents one region's contribution, and the full bar height represents the combined total revenue for that month across all territories.
data.code: SELECT CAST(f.MonthNum AS INTEGER) AS MonthNum, CASE CAST(f.MonthNum AS INTEGER) WHEN 1 THEN 'January' WHEN 2 THEN 'February' WHEN 3 THEN 'March' WHEN 4 THEN 'April' WHEN 5 THEN 'May' WHEN 6 THEN 'June' WHEN 7 THEN 'July' WHEN 8 THEN 'August' WHEN 9 THEN 'September' WHEN 10 THEN 'October' WHEN 11 THEN 'November' WHEN 12 THEN 'December' END AS MonthName, r.RegionName, SUM(f.TotalRevenue_GBP) AS Revenue_GBP FROM fact_financial_summary f JOIN dim_region r ON f.RegionID = r.RegionID WHERE f.Year = 2024 GROUP BY CAST(f.MonthNum AS INTEGER), MonthName, r.RegionName ORDER BY MonthNum
insights: Edinburgh consistently leads revenue, peaking at £19,051 in May — highest single region-month figure.
Bristol and Cardiff are the lowest contributors each month, rarely exceeding £10,500.
Monthly total revenue grew from ~£119,938 in January to ~£140,542 in May, a ~17% increase.
Manchester surged to £17,629 in April, its strongest month, up 35% from January's £12,322.
recommendations: Investigate Edinburgh and Birmingham's growth drivers and replicate tactics in Bristol and Cardiff.
Target January-to-February dip months with promotional campaigns to sustain early-year momentum.
Set Q3 benchmarks using May's total as a baseline to track continued revenue growth trajectory.
data.forecast: Revenue shows a consistent upward trend from January through May across most regions, suggesting H2 totals could surpass H1 if current momentum holds. Edinburgh and Manchester's strong growth trajectories position them as key drivers for full-year performance.

marcus.title: What is the average revenue per session type? Show all session types ranked from highest to lowest as a horizontal bar chart.

data.title: Average Revenue per Session Type (Highest to Lowest)
data.explanation: This shows the average revenue generated per completed consultation, ranked by service type. Higher-value services like combined packages and workshops tend to generate the most revenue per session.
data.code: SELECT ServiceName, ROUND(AVG(RevenueActual_GBP), 2) AS AvgRevenue_GBP FROM fact_consultations WHERE Status = 'Completed' GROUP BY ServiceName ORDER BY AvgRevenue_GBP DESC
insights: Colour & Style Combined leads at £425, nearly 42% higher than the second-ranked Personal Shopping (£300).
Top 4 services (£250+) generate significantly more than the remaining 8, revealing a clear revenue tier split.
Group Colour Workshop (£90) and Colour Fan Replacement (£50) anchor the bottom, pulling overall averages down.
Online Colour Analysis (£150) earns less than in-person Colour Analysis (£290) — a £140 gap per session.
recommendations: Upsell Colour Analysis clients to the Combined package to capture the £135 revenue uplift per session.
Review pricing or bundling for Group Colour Workshop and Colour Fan Replacement to improve their yield.
Promote Personal Shopping and Wardrobe Edit services more actively as high-value, under-leveraged offerings.

data.title: Dylan James — June 2023 Revenue by Service
data.explanation: This breaks down Dylan James's June 2023 revenue by service type, showing which services contributed most to his total revenue that month.
data.code: SELECT s.ServiceName, SUM(fc.RevenueActual_GBP) AS revenue FROM fact_consultations fc JOIN dim_stylist ds ON fc.StylistID = ds.StylistID JOIN dim_service s ON fc.ServiceID = s.ServiceID WHERE ds.StylistName = 'Dylan James' AND fc.Year = 2023 AND fc.MonthNum = '06' GROUP BY s.ServiceName ORDER BY revenue DESC
insights: Colour Analysis is Dylan James's top service in June 2023 at £1,463.86, leading all categories.
Colour & Style Combined is a close second at £1,308.93, together these two account for ~57% of total revenue.
Online Colour Analysis contributes £614.18, showing meaningful demand for remote offerings.
Group Colour Workshop is the lowest earner at £106.47, roughly 14x less than top service.
recommendations: Promote Colour & Style Combined bundles further, as high revenue suggests strong client appetite for combined services.
Expand Online Colour Analysis capacity to capture remote clients and grow this £614 revenue stream.
Investigate low Group Workshop uptake and consider targeted marketing or pricing adjustments to boost volume.
